grammar.topic: Verbs that change meaning: stop, remember, forget, try, regret
explainTr: Bazı fiillerden sonra to + fiil ile -ing farklı anlam verir. stop + -ing: bir şeyi bırakmak (She stopped talking: konuşmayı kesti). stop + to + fiil: başka bir şey yapmak için durmak (She stopped to talk: konuşmak için durdu).

remember/forget + to + fiil: yapılacak şeyi hatırlamak/unutmak (Remember to lock the door). remember/forget + -ing: yapılmış şeyi hatırlamak/unutmamak (I remember locking it). regret + to + fiil: üzülerek söylemek (I regret to tell you...); regret + -ing: yaptığına pişman olmak (I regret shouting).
try + to + fiil: çabalamak, denemek zor olan şeyi (I tried to open it). try + -ing: sonucu görmek için bir yöntemi denemek (Try opening the window). Sınıf yönetiminde bu farkı sık kullanırsın.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'kapıyı kilitlemeyi unuttum' ve 'kapıyı kilitlediğimi unutmadım' fiil çekimiyle ayrılır. İngilizcede aynı fiil iki kalıpla farklı anlam verir: forget to lock (yapmadım), forget locking (yaptım ama unuttum).

reading.title: Learning from a veteran teacher
reading.text:
On Monday, Hafsa observed Ms. Dunn's third-grade class for two hours. She sat at the back with a notebook and tried writing down everything that helped the teacher keep the room calm.

The first thing she noticed was Ms. Dunn's routine. Every morning, students enter, hang their jackets, and begin a short writing task. "If they are busy in the first five minutes, I rarely need to discipline anyone," Ms. Dunn explained later. Around ten o'clock, two boys began talking loudly. Instead of shouting, Ms. Dunn stopped speaking and stood quietly beside them. The boys stopped talking almost at once and looked up. She smiled and said, "Thank you. Please remember to raise your hand when you have something to share."

Later a girl kept forgetting to bring her pencil. Ms. Dunn did not scold her. She tried giving her a small job, handing out papers, and the girl became more focused. "I tried reminding her many times," Ms. Dunn said, "but a responsibility works better than a warning."

Hafsa also noticed how consistent the teacher was. The same expectations applied to everyone, and the consequences were always calm and predictable. When a student crossed the boundary, Ms. Dunn spoke in a firm but kind tone and offered a choice: finish the task now or finish it during recess. She never regretted setting clear limits. "I remember trying to be everyone's friend during my first year," she said. "It was exhausting, and the class got louder every day."

At the end of the day, Ms. Dunn gave Hafsa a piece of advice. "When you substitute, don't forget to learn the names quickly. Use a seating chart and monitor the room by walking around. Stop and look at students who are off task rather than calling across the room. Most of the time, a quiet cue is enough."

Hafsa wrote the tips on the first page of her notebook. She realized that classroom management was not about being strict. It was about being predictable, patient, and prepared, and she felt she could learn all three.

questions.q: What advice did Ms. Dunn give to substitutes?
options: Learn the names quickly and use a seating chart.
questions.whyTr: Metin: 'learn the names quickly. Use a seating chart'.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Ms. Dunn, I tried using your quiet-cue trick today.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Surprisingly well. I stopped talking, and the class became silent in ten seconds.

script.speaker: Ms. Dunn
script.text: Wonderful. Did you remember to praise them afterward?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Unfortunately I forgot to do that. I only remembered when the bell rang.

script.speaker: Ms. Dunn

script.speaker: Hafsa

script.speaker: Ms. Dunn

script.speaker: Hafsa

script.speaker: Ms. Dunn

script.speaker: Ms. Dunn
script.text: Perfect. That's the best habit a substitute can have.

writing.promptTr: Yeni bir vekil öğretmene sınıf yönetimi tavsiyeleri yaz. En az üç fiil kalıbı kullan: remember to, stop + -ing, try + -ing, regret + -ing, forget to. 120-180 kelime yaz.
writing.promptEn: Write advice to a new substitute teacher. Use at least three of these: remember to, stop + -ing, try + -ing, regret + -ing, forget to.
writing.model: Dear new substitute, here are some tips from my own experience. First, remember to arrive early and read the sub plan carefully. I once forgot to check the seating chart, and I regret losing the first ten minutes of the day. When the class gets noisy, try standing quietly in front of the room instead of shouting. Students usually stop talking after a few seconds. If one child keeps interrupting, stop and speak to him privately. Don't forget to praise good behavior as well. I remember seeing how a small compliment changed a whole lesson. At the end of the day, remember to leave a note for the regular teacher, and try describing both the good moments and the problems. If you follow these steps, you will probably feel more confident very quickly. Please come to my room if you need anything. I am always happy to help, and I know that nobody forgets their first day as a substitute. Good luck! Hafsa
checklistTr: En az üç kalıp kullandın mı (remember to, try -ing, stop -ing...)?
Yapılacak şeyler için 'to + fiil', geçmiş deneyim için '-ing' kullandın mı?
Anlam farkını doğru yansıttın mı (stop to / stop -ing)?
